Philadelphia is one of the friendlier big cities for couch disposal: the Streets Department treats sofas as "compactible furniture," which means they go out with your **regular weekly trash, no appointment, up to two large items per week.** The traps are timing and what counts as compactible.

## The Streets Department Rules, Exactly

- **Sofas, loveseats, and chairs go out on your regular trash day**, up to two large items per week, no scheduling needed.
- **Set-out windows are seasonal.** Spring and summer (April through September): between 7 PM the evening before and 7 AM on collection day. Fall and winter: from 5 PM the evening before. Center City runs its own rules, so check yours.
- **Mattresses and box springs must be sealed in plastic mattress bags**, which matters if your couch is a sleeper.
- **Metal oversized items and appliances are not collected curbside.** Those go to a Sanitation Convenience Center, free with proof of residency, Monday through Saturday.
- **A newer option:** the city's Residential Bulk Collection program lets you schedule a pickup through 311 or the online portal, up to four items per appointment, for single-family homes and buildings up to six units.
- The stakes for getting it wrong are real: Pennsylvania law allows illegal-dumping fines up to $5,000, and the city runs camera enforcement.

## When the Curb Isn't the Answer

Rowhouse Philadelphia has a specific problem the free program doesn't touch: **the carry.** A sectional down a 19th-century staircase, or anything out of a third-floor trinity, is your job before the truck ever arrives. Timing is the other gap: your trash day rarely matches your lease end.

And a good couch deserves better than the curb. Philadelphia has strong donation options, including Uhuru Furniture, Habitat ReStore, and Philly AIDS Thrift, each with [condition standards](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/).

When those gaps matter: [couch removal in Philadelphia](/pa/philadelphia/couch-removal/) starts at $90 with the carry-out included, [same-day in most ZIPs when booked before 2PM local time](/book-online/), and [donation pickup](/pa/philadelphia/donation-pickup/) routes good furniture to local partners. Pricing by item is in the [cost guide](/blog/junk-removal/how-much-does-couch-removal-cost/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Philadelphia pick up couches for free?

Yes. Sofas count as compactible furniture and go out with regular weekly trash, up to two large items per week, with no appointment. The city also offers scheduled bulk pickups through 311.

### When can I put a couch out in Philadelphia?

Only in the set-out window the evening before your collection day: after 7 PM in spring and summer, after 5 PM in fall and winter, and gone by 7 AM collection morning. Earlier than that is a violation.

### Does Philadelphia take metal furniture or appliances at the curb?

No. Metal oversized items, appliances, and tires are excluded from curbside collection and go to a Sanitation Convenience Center instead.

### What's the fastest way to remove a couch in Philadelphia?

Booked removal: [same-day across most of Philadelphia](/pa/philadelphia/couch-removal/) when booked before 2PM local time, carried from inside your home, stairs included when noted at booking.
